en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-Dizang-pusa-dharani-sutra*.

Thus have I heard. At one time the Buddha was staying on Mount Kharatīya, at the abode of the ṛṣi Muni, together with a great assembly of bhikṣus and an immeasurable, incalculable multitude of śrāvakas.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable.
Having finished explaining the Candragarbha [Sūtra],
at that time, a great fragrant cloud rained down from the south.
A great rain of incense;
a rain of great clouds of flowers;
a rain of great flowers.
An immeasurable rain of necklaces and clouds of various necklaces;
a rain of great robes and clouds of robes.
A great rain fell.
At the dwelling place of the Sage Seer on Mount Khadiraka,
all these great rains completely filled [the area].
Great clouds rained down fragrant flowers, garments, and necklaces, while various and immeasurable sounds of the Dharma were also proclaimed.
Thus it continues in sequence, extensively described,
up to the sound of the Three Refuges.
The sound of upholding the precepts;
the sound of patience;
the sound of diligence.
The sound of meditative concentration;
the sound of possessing perfect wisdom that subdues the four māras;
the sound of whose fame is universally heard, pervading the three realms.
The sound of mindfulness, concentration, and dhāraṇī;
the sound of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness;
the sound of detachment from desire.
Form is like the sound of a mass of foam;
feeling is like the sound of a water bubble;
perception is like the sound of a mirage.
The sound of formations is like that of a plantain tree;
the sound of consciousness is like that of a magical illusion;
and there is the sound of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self.
The sound of shame and remorse;
the sound of the foundations of mindfulness;
the sound of loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.
The sound of realizing all phenomena;
the sound of nirvana being without a dwelling place;
the sound of the three vehicles.
The sound of turning the wheel of Dharma;
the sound of bringing sentient beings to maturity;
the sound of delivering them from the three evil realms.
The sound of the six pāramitās;
the sound of skillful means up to the fulfillment of the ten stages;
and the sound of sporting in supernatural powers.
The sound of sporting in the unsurpassed Mahāyāna;
the sound of non-retrogression (*avaivartika*);
the sound of the patient acceptance of the non-arising of phenomena (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*).
They entered the ocean-like sound of the Buddha;
all those who had gathered beheld various rains and also heard the sounds of immeasurable dharmas.
There was the sound of garments being adorned according to their wishes.
Furthermore, they all saw that in each of their two hands there were wish-fulfilling jewels (*cintāmaṇi*) raining down wish-fulfilling treasures;
each of these wish-fulfilling jewels emitted its own radiance.
Within these lights, one sees all the Buddhas of the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions;
each of these Buddhas is surrounded by their own assembly of bodhisattvas.
Within that radiance, one sees all the Buddha-worlds of the ten directions.
Should there be any who are ill,
once they are touched by the light, their various ailments will be cured and healed.
All those who are bound by fetters and those who are destined for death shall all attain liberation through the touch of this light upon their bodies.
Even those who have committed evil deeds of body, evil deeds of speech, and evil deeds of mind [shall be liberated].
When the light touches their bodies, it completely eliminates the three evil realms.
If sentient beings suffering from hunger and thirst receive the touch of this light, they all become fully satiated.
Those who undergo various forms of punishment and experience intense physical suffering—
Those who lack clothing, ornaments, necklaces, or various such items,
upon being touched by this light, shall have all their needs fulfilled according to their thoughts.
Likewise, those who have committed killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, lying, frivolous speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, or verbal abuse— once touched by this light— [shall be purified].
All such evils as these are entirely eliminated.
Among all sentient beings, there is the suffering of not obtaining what one seeks;
when they are touched by this light, they all experience happiness.
The light is pure and entirely free from obscuration;
winds, clouds, dust, mist, and all defilements, afflictions, bitterness, and sorrow, as well as unwholesome sounds,
even up to fearsome and evil tactile sensations, are all extinguished.
They remain far removed from all evils;
all forms of deceit, falsehood, and crookedness are likewise eliminated without exception,
and all evil desires are entirely cast aside.
All manner of sublime and supreme joys gathered together.
At that time, the entire assembly became firm and unshakable,
as immovable as the earth.
The mind has no coming or going and cannot be destroyed.
It was unprecedented for this great assembly that,
for what reason and by what causal condition, our bodies have now all become so heavy that we cannot support ourselves?
At that time, there was a Śakra named Viśuddhasattva,
who was seated not far from the great assembly.
Thereupon, Viśuddhavatī rose from her seat,
adjusted her robes, knelt with her right knee on the ground,
joined her palms toward the Buddha, and questioned him in verse:
Speaker of truth, seer of truth, the Muni, the Honored One,
who dwells in truth and has long abided in the practice of the Dharma— may you please expound the Dharma;
for the Buddha is the true cause and condition that can extinguish the suffering of sentient beings.
For what reason does it rain down various rains here,
causing the great assembly to rejoice? By revealing all doubts and bestowing the peace of faith upon their minds,
you cause them to abide in the Mahāyāna.
His body is as immovable as the earth; all humans and devas alike perceive such a sign.
The great assembly is filled with doubt, for from each of his two hands there emerges the radiance of mani jewels.
All garments and garlands, Various ornaments and articles for adorning the body—
The field of merit for the ten directions, Free from all faults and evils,
where all sufferings find rest— All are due to the Savior of the World.
Among all the devas and humans, none are able to explain the causes and conditions:
whose supernormal power is this that has brought [them] here?
It is for the sake of the Buddha and the bodhisattvas, as well as Brahmā, Māra, and Śakra.
“I only pray that the Savior of the World will explain the causes and conditions of these supernormal powers.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Śakra, the Lord of the Pure Realm, saying: “It is so, it is so.”
Listen attentively now;
I shall explain it to you.
This Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha, throughout immeasurable asaṃkhyeya kalpas...
He has come here for the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity in this world of the five turbidities,
accompanied by eighty *bimbara* *nayuta* hundreds of thousands of *koṭi*s of great bodhisattvas.
It was entirely for the purpose of paying homage, making offerings, and showing respect;
it was because he wished to see the great assembly gathered together and wished to hear the great assembly express their sympathetic joy.
This was the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha appearing in the form of a śramaṇa;
through the manifestation of his supernormal powers,
he produced such great displays of majestic adornment.
It is also the inconceivable and immeasurable merit of the Tathāgata;
it is called the true Dharma-treasury of the śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas;
and it is called the great jewel-mine of the treasure of liberating wisdom.
It is also called the Bodhisattva’s Dharma for saving the world;
it is also called the Guide and Caravan Leader to Nirvana;
it is like a wish-fulfilling jewel that satisfies all that is sought.
It is like a jewel casket for all merchants;
it is like the great earth, capable of producing roots of goodness;
and it is a sacred vessel for seeking the Dharma in order to attain nirvāṇa.
It is also a vessel of pure merit;
it is also the sphere of illumination for the sun and moon;
and it is also a great torch for the darkness of deep obscurity.
It is like the moon cooling the heat of afflictions;
it is like one without feet obtaining a wish-fulfilling vehicle;
it is like one with a distracted mind attaining the taste of nectar.
It is like a frail old person encountering a stool and a staff;
it is the very foundation of the great field of merit.
Let the mind of renunciation be free from stagnation.
It is like a subsequent current that rescues one from suffering and hardship;
it is like the rising of a cloud-canopy of kinsmen and friends that dispels the flames of the fetters;
it is like a water-purifying jewel that removes turbidity and impurity.
If one encounters treacherous turns, it shows the correct path;
for those who are utterly exhausted, it is a peaceful forest seat;
it is the bridge over the four swift currents of birth and death.
It is also the supreme great ship for crossing to the other shore;
it is the sublime and wondrous fruit of these three roots of goodness;
it is the most excellent Mahāyāna for all who practice giving.
His upholding of the precepts is as immovable as Mount Sumeru;
his diligence is as indestructible as a diamond;
and his patience is as firm and solid as the great earth.
Upholding the True Dharma, his mind is free from the three marks;
adorned with meditative concentration like a wondrous flower garland,
his wisdom is profound and vast like the great ocean.
The mind has no basis, like empty space;
skillful means are untainted, like a cluster of flowers;
he dwells among those of external paths like a lion king.
He remains far removed from afflictions like the single horn of a rhinoceros;
he extinguishes all fetters and latent tendencies as if washing away dust and grime;
and he is able to dispel foul odors like a swift, driving wind.
He protects those who are ill like a skilled physician;
he eliminates all maladies like a sovereign medicinal king;
and he cuts away afflictions like one wielding a sharp sword.
For those who are terrified, he acts as a great kinsman;
he defends against all enemies like a firm city with its moats;
and he can remove their turbidity like pure water.
It relieves the hunger and deprivation of others like a succulent fruit;
it is the most excellent garment for those who are naked,
and serves as a dense cloud-canopy for those scorched by intense heat.
Possessing such fruits and rewards of these roots of goodness,
they are supremely pure, firm, and indestructible;
in the realm of exquisite forms, they are able to give rise to the experience of bliss.
One gives rise to a sense of shame and remorse within the great assembly,
eliminates all fetters and afflictions,
and, in the sphere of meditative concentration, mounts the four right efforts.
The four means of integration and the decisive flow of patience are like the great earth;
the profound and vast dhāraṇīs are like the great ocean;
and the unimpeded, sovereign supernormal powers are like space.
Having subdued all māras and all habitual tendencies,
they practice the right path and immeasurable meditative concentrations,
and they also serve as an island of refuge for all kinds of wisdom.
He is able to turn the unsurpassed, pure wheel of Dharma.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha has manifested these auspicious signs in advance because he wishes to come;
furthermore, he has come here for the purpose of making offerings to and honoring me.
The Buddha again praised Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, saying:
"You have come from the south,
accompanied by eighty *bimbara* hundreds of thousands of *nayuta* bodhisattvas, all arriving here together through their supernormal powers."
They all assumed the appearance of śrāvakas before the Tathāgata,
prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right,
and then, with palms joined, spoke these verses:
The supreme Great Guide among two-legged beings, Who constantly cultivates loving-kindness and gives rise to a virtuous mind;
Who can produce patience like the great earth, Liberating sentient beings and removing their anger;
Endowed with the most supreme marks and signs, He is able to adorn all realms.
They are able to fulfill all fields of merit, Constantly practicing truthful speech and great compassion;
They are able to completely sever the net of all sensations, And are all able to dwell well in reality as it is.
Leaving behind other pure Buddha-lands, The sentient beings therein possess roots of goodness.
By his original vow, he desires to deliver the world of turbid evil, To bring all sentient beings to fulfillment,
And to give rise to firm and diligent vigor, Surpassing immeasurable ascetic practices.
He constantly cultivates difficult and terrifying paths, Surpassing immeasurable ascetic practices.
Through generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, The cultivation of meditative concentration and wisdom,
I make offerings to the countless Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, As well as the great assembly of Śrāvakas;
Providing for all their needs— food, drink, and medicine for the sick— I deliver all beings from every form of bondage.
Since beginningless time, I have sacrificed my body and life for the benefit of sentient beings without any greed or attachment;
for the sake of the Dharma, I have constantly sacrificed my body, giving my skin, flesh, bones, and blood to all beings.
I have relinquished all the happiness I have attained, possessing great compassion for the sake of all.
Regarding the net of afflictions of all sentient beings, they practice tranquility and completely transcend them;
they open and close all six sense faculties and are always able to remain far removed from all desires.
They cultivate the contemplations of suffering, impermanence, emptiness, and non-self, and are also well-versed in observing conventional truth.
The root cause of all suffering is craving; He is able to completely dry up all afflictions.
For this reason, he gathers in the six sense-faculties, And is able to skillfully sever all desire.
He is able to cultivate the gateways of immeasurable great compassion, Universally bestowing [benefit] upon all living beings.
I shall not abandon my great vow, nor shall I dwell in the supreme enlightenment;
seeing that all sentient beings are like those born blind and suffer most acutely,
I contemplate for their sake and am thus able to diligently practice great vigor.
You have generated transcendent diligence in giving, morality, and patience, and cultivated all meditative concentrations as well as wisdom;
just as a mother nurtures her only child with a heart of loving-kindness,
so too do you toward all sentient beings, constantly able to provide for them all.
Therefore, you shall swiftly attain enlightenment and deliver all immeasurable multitudes of beings.
When you originally practiced for the sake of awakening, you vowed not to abandon a single sentient being;
thus, you have constantly abided in generosity, ethical discipline, and patience, as well as in diligence, meditative concentration, and the cultivation of wisdom.
Those who are always able, within that final age, to seek the unsurpassed,
supreme Bodhi— therefore, as saviors of the world in the final kalpa, they swiftly attain the unsurpassed, most excellent path;
they subdue the evil Māras, yakṣas, and others, as well as all wicked nāgas, spirits, and humans.
Like a vajra that severs all fetters, you are able to establish all beings securely upon the noble paths;
you bestow predictions of enlightenment upon immeasurable multitudes, destined for the unsurpassed path of Bodhi.
O one of supreme merit, wisdom, and clear insight, you are the great general of the true field of merit.
To save the world throughout immeasurable realms, they provide shelter for all living beings;
as fields of merit throughout the worlds of the ten directions, their fame is heard afar, pervading everywhere.
For this reason, all bodhisattvas are able to relinquish their own affairs entirely.
You have gathered here by means of your supernormal powers; All together approach the World-Honored One, the Great Muni.
I pray that the Tathāgata will specially expound the teaching, So that all who hear it may rejoice.
Having heard the Dharma, they shall apply themselves with diligent effort, Constantly cultivating and training in the path to Bodhi.
All are like the great power of the ocean generals; they shall swiftly draw near to Bodhi.
This great assembly has never been heard of or seen before.
Therefore, you all have come together to this gathering—thirteen billion yakṣas who are cruel and devour flesh and blood.
Swiftly abandoning all evils, they have arrived here, Abiding securely in the most supreme and unsurpassed path.
Some have attained the dhāraṇī of patience; Some have attained the most wondrous meditative concentrations.
Some have already realized the exhaustion of all outflows— Unattached Arhats, the Honored Ones among men.
There are those who can skillfully cultivate the four immeasurables; There are those who can abide in the four means of integration;
There are those who have attained the four supreme analytical knowledges; And there are those who have attained the cultivation of the various dharmas of patience.
There are those who have attained the Śūraṅgama Samādhi; And there are those who have attained the eye of wisdom that is like space.
There are those who have attained the patient acceptance of the non-arising of all phenomena; all this is due to the Dharma taught by the World-Honored One.

He has completely subdued all heterodox teachers—the ninety-six kinds of external paths—and having crushed all enemies and Māras, all this is through the power of the Great General who saves the world.
He opens and closes the realms of hell, hungry ghosts, and animals, Benefiting all the multitudes of devas and humans;
Therefore, all true sentient beings have gathered here through the Buddha’s spiritual power.
The kalpas of famine, plague, and warfare are all extinguished this very day.
If there are those who are blind and ignorant, having lost the right path, and these sentient beings are tormented by immeasurable afflictions and madness—

may they all be established upon the path of quiescent extinction so that the multitude may all be able to abandon their own karmic deeds; it is for the sake of paying homage to the Tathāgata that we have come here.
In immeasurable worlds and billions of Buddha-fields, there dwell those who save the world;
their fame is heard throughout the ten directions as immeasurable.
Having heard this, we have come here to this ocean of merit of all-knowledge, to hear such true characteristics as these.
To deliver all sentient beings, I pay homage so that they may be filled with joy;
throughout hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of kalpas, I shall constantly and diligently practice various forms of giving.
Now I shall train myself to give rise to great vows; I have now come here through the Buddha’s supernormal power.
"I shall practice and train in this place of turbid worlds, so as to be able to reach the foremost, supreme Bodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Kṣitigarbha scattered various kinds of celestial flowers, incense, and flower garlands over the Buddha.
The flowers that were scattered transformed into jeweled canopies.
At that time, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva sat before the Buddha,
listening attentively and receiving the sutra.
The assembly gathered there, seeing Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
conceived a sense of rare wonder and offered various kinds of incense, flowers, necklaces, silk canopies, banners, pennants, and garments.
They scattered [the flowers] over the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha and spoke these words:
"We have truly obtained great and wholesome benefit."
By the spiritual power of the Buddha, they were able to see these great beings (mahāpuruṣa),
whom they paid homage to, saluted,
and inquired after their well-being. At that time, there was also the bodhisattva mahāsattva Tr̥ṣṇāvatī.
Rising from his seat,
he adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground,
joined his palms toward the Buddha, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, from which buddha-field has this son of good family come here?
What roots of goodness has he cultivated that he is able to offer such various praises and speak of the Buddha’s merits?”
"I have never heard or seen such a thing since the distant past.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Thirsting for Aspiration:
"Cease, cease, O Mahāsattva!"
There is no need for this to be heard by the entire assembly and the devas and humans;
with the exception of the Buddha-Tathāgata, there is no one capable of knowing the measure of the merit of this son of good family.
The Tathāgata shall surely proclaim this today.
However, the devas and humans are obscured by their own ignorance and darkness.
This son of noble family has accomplished the inconceivable merit of the Śūraṅgama Samādhi.
Entering the sphere of activity of the Tathāgatas, they attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti).
They attain mastery over all Buddha-dharmas.
Having entered the profound patience of dharmas, they cross the ocean of all-knowledge.
This son of good family sports in the Lion’s Light Samādhi;
ascending the peak of Mount Sumeru, the mountain of omniscience,
he subdues those of heterodox views and brings sentient beings to fulfillment.
They dwell in all Buddha-fields;
they enter the samādhi of wisdom into whichever Buddha-field they may be in.
By the power of this samādhi, they [attain this].
May all sentient beings in all lands behold the bodhisattvas,
who enter the samādhi of the joy of wisdom in accordance with the buddha-fields,
and perform all offerings to the Buddhas within those lands.
Following the various Buddha-lands, he enters the Samādhi of Pure Joy.
Upon entering this samādhi, he perceives all the faults of every desire;
yet, within the characteristics of his mind, he remains pure and untainted.
Entering the samādhi of shame and remorse in accordance with all buddha-fields,
he causes all sentient beings in those lands to attain shame and remorse, thereby remaining far removed from all evils and free from the darkness of ignorance.
He enters the *samādhi* of entering the whirlpools of all Buddha-lands,
and is also able to cause all those sentient beings to enter this same concentration,
enabling them to attain the knowledge of past lives.
He was able to die in this life and be reborn in that;
he was skilled in meditative concentration,
entering the Samādhi of Sorrowless Radiance in accordance with all lands.
He is also able to cause all those sentient beings to be entirely free from sorrow and grief;
he enters the samādhi of supernatural powers within the various Buddha-lands,
and is also able to cause all those sentient beings to enter the samādhi of supernatural powers.
Following the Buddha’s lands, he enters the Samādhi of Wisdom-Light;
he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to be entirely free from ignorance,
whereupon they behold all the Buddha-lands of the ten directions.
He enters the Buddha-torch samādhi in accordance with all buddha-fields,
and is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to take refuge in the Triple Gem.
He enters the vajra-light samādhi in accordance with all buddha-fields.
Having entered this samādhi,
he is also able to cause all those buddha-fields,
including the Iron Ring Mountains and the Iron Encircling Mountains, [to appear].
Even unto Mount Sumeru, the King of Mountains,
all ravines, gullies, and chasms appeared completely;
the ground was as level as the palm of a hand.
It can cause all evil venomous snakes and malevolent sorcery to be completely extinguished.
Following the Buddha-lands, it enters the Samādhi of the Power of Wisdom for Subjugation;
it can also cause those Māras and their retinues to be utterly terrified and take refuge in the Triple Gem.
Entering the *Vidyutprabhā-samādhi* in accordance with the various Buddha-fields,
he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to be free from fear of future lives and to attain the consolation of the Dharma.
Entering the *Sukha-samādhi* in accordance with the various Buddha-fields...
Furthermore, he is able to cause all those sentient beings to obtain sufficient food and drink according to their thoughts;
he enters the Samādhi of Vital Essence and Joyful Delight in accordance with the various Buddha-lands.
It can also cause all those sentient beings to attain a firm and stable body, free from all suffering of illness,
and to enter the Samādhi of Entering All Buddha-lands with Requisites of Joy;
it can also cause all those sentient beings.
They fully obtain bedding, clothing, and ornaments spread out for them, lacking nothing;
their illnesses are treated with medicine, and their bodies are all upright and handsome.
They enter the samādhi of non-contentious wisdom in accordance with the various Buddha-lands.
It can also cause the bodies of all those sentient beings to become long, adorned, dignified, and magnificent;
it causes them to be far removed from all enmity, hatred, and bondage,
so that they all experience happiness.
In all respects, they were like those who practice generosity, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, and meditative concentration;
their minds were undistracted, they were fully endowed with wisdom, and they deeply penetrated the characteristics of phenomena.
Following the various Buddha-lands, they entered the samādhi of freedom from sorrow and fear.
And he is able to cause all those sentient beings to attain a heart of joy, free from sorrow and fear.
Following the various Buddha-lands, he enters the Samādhi of Radiant Bliss;
in those Buddha-lands, all sentient beings attain unimpeded wisdom and are freed from worldly affairs.
Entering the Well-Abiding Vajra Samādhi in accordance with all Buddha-fields,
he is also able to cause all sentient beings therein to attain the full perfection of their faculties, none of which shall be deficient or impaired.
Following the Buddha-lands, he enters the Samādhi of the Banner of Contemplation;
he is also able to cause all those sentient beings to become weary of and detached from all evils, to abandon them, and to uphold the ten wholesome paths so as to be reborn in the heavenly realms.
Following the buddha-fields, they enter deeply into the samādhi of the voice of great compassion;
they are also able to cause all those sentient beings to feel mutual pity for one another and give rise to hearts of loving-kindness.
They attain a mind of fearlessness, a mind free from affliction, and an impartial mind, regarding one another with compassion.
Following the various Buddha-fields, they enter the *saṃbhāra-samādhi* (Samādhi of the Accumulation of Merit).
They are also able to cause all those sentient beings to become free from strife and contention.
Diseases, famines, unseasonable winds and rains, and the bitter and sour flavors of suffering in food and drink are all completely extinguished.
This is because the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha has entered the Samādhi of Oceanic Lightning in that Buddha-field.
In whatever land he arrived, everything was transformed into a ground of jewels;
adorned with trees of fine garments, trees of necklaces,
and trees of flowers and fruits, the Buddha-realm was magnificently embellished.
At the time of dawn, he entered the samādhi of the worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges;
for the sake of bringing sentient beings to maturity, he arose from that meditative concentration,
causing immeasurable and boundless Buddha-worlds to [manifest].
In this world of the five turbidities, he brings sentient beings to maturity;
and when the calamity of war breaks out in all Buddha-worlds without exception,
this son of noble family, by the power of entering samādhi at the time of dawn, [accomplishes his task].
Weapons, armor, and staffs shall all be completely extinguished.
Should epidemics arise in any Buddha-field to harm sentient beings,
those epidemics shall likewise be naturally extinguished.
In whichever Buddha-fields famines may arise,
he causes those famines to be completely extinguished and all beings to attain full satisfaction;
this is because of the majestic spiritual power of this son of good family’s samādhi.
He is able to bring all sentient beings to fulfillment.
Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva brings sentient beings to fulfillment through inconceivable merit.
At the abodes of immeasurable Buddhas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the past, he has performed this work.
They have made firm vows of great compassion to bring all sentient beings to complete fulfillment;
their power of adornment is like a flash of lightning.
Within the duration of a single meal, they are able to bring to fulfillment the roots of goodness of immeasurable billions of nayutas of beings.
If there are sentient beings tormented by immeasurable varieties of suffering, or pressed by the urgency of hunger and thirst;
For those who invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha,
he is able to ensure that they have sufficient food and drink, extinguish all their sufferings and afflictions,
and establish them on the path to nirvāṇa so that they all attain happiness.
If there are sentient beings who lack clothing, jeweled crowns, necklaces, medicinal treatments for illness and emaciation, or various other necessities,
and they invoke the name of the Bodhisattva Kṣitigarbha, [their needs shall be fulfilled].
He causes all that they desire to be fully provided;
they abide in the path to nirvāṇa and attain the supreme bliss.
If there are sentient beings who are separated from a mind of joy and bliss and are gathered together with those who lack such joy and bliss, [he brings them to fulfillment].
If one invokes the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva,
all instruments of pleasure shall come entirely to them,
and whatever they do not delight in shall likewise be completely removed.
Those who so desire shall all be enabled to dwell securely in nirvana and attain the supreme bliss.
If there are sentient beings whose bodies and minds suffer and who are afflicted by various diseases, [they shall likewise be relieved].
Those who are able to recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva will have all physical and mental suffering and affliction completely eliminated and healed;
they shall be established in nirvāṇa and attain the supreme bliss.
If any sentient beings harbor malicious intentions toward one another,
yet are able to recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion,
he shall cause those beings to become gentle and patient, and to feel mutual shame and remorse.
Through the repentance of a compassionate heart, one dwells securely in nirvana.
If there are sentient beings who are imprisoned, confined in dungeons, or bound with shackles upon their bodies, and they undergo all manner of suffering,
yet are able to recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion;
May all sentient beings attain liberation, sovereignty, and non-obstruction;
even those who ought to be bound and subjected to the whip or staff, if they can recite the name of Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva and take refuge with single-minded devotion, [shall be released].
In this same way, they all attained liberation,
